label: Seeking or resting in the intellectually apprehended good belongs to will
summary: The analogy with a thing’s orientation to its natural perfection supports will in an intellectual nature and its application to God. In God the text ascribes love and delight in the possessed good, with no deficiency implied. I q.80 a.2 describes passive appetite in the soul. I q.82 a.1 ad 2 calls will intellectual insofar as it wills something naturally. That reply starts with will already in view.
blocker: The body treats intellectually apprehended good as an object of will, rather than requiring deficient seeking. Applying this to the target requires every appetitive principle satisfying FollowsIntellect to amount to that orientation to intellectually apprehended good, and the orientation to warrant HasWill for the same bearer without treating divine willing as a distinct passive capacity.
